extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom leaders, media researchers, policymakers, and the informed public interested in digital news consumption
extracted.subtask_description: A report analysing how audiences consume, trust, pay for, avoid, and interact with digital news across countries, based on a large YouGov survey and complementary qualitative research. It covers platform use (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube), attitudes to AI, influencers, payment behaviour and cross‑country comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news
rubrics_metrics.description: How audiences think about trust in news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes measures such as percentage who 'trust most news most of the time' with country-level comparisons (e.g., Hungary and Greece at 23%, the lowest in the sample). Used as a core indicator of news credibility and public confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform importance in news consumption and production
rubrics_metrics.description: The growing importance of platforms in news consumption and production, including more visual and video-led social media such as TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses which platforms people use for news and how platforms reshape audience interaction with news; includes specific platform usage rates by country (e.g., TikTok use for news highest in Thailand 39% and Kenya 36%).

rubrics_metrics.name: News avoidance / news fatigue
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of news avoidance and feelings of being worn out by the news agenda
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks changes over time and across countries (e.g., Spain: people feeling worn out up from 26% in 2019 to 44% in 2024; Argentina: up to 45% avoid the news). Used to evaluate audience engagement and potential reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concerns about misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels of concern among audiences about misinformation in news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported alongside news avoidance; used to gauge public perceptions of information quality and the perceived reliability of news sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public attitudes towards AI in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Public attitudes about AI and journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores audience views on the use of generative AI in news, supported by a supplementary report ('OK computer? Understanding public attitudes towards the uses of generative AI in news') that uses qualitative research to illuminate reactions and concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and influence of creators and news influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: What we know about the rise of news influencers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the role creators and influencers play in news dissemination and audience trust/engagement; examines how influencer content intersects with traditional news provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for news / willingness to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: How much do people pay for news? And what might encourage more people to pay?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures current payment behaviour and tests potential incentives to increase paid news subscriptions or one-off payments; used to assess commercial sustainability models for news organisations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest in news (change over time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels of interest in news and trends over time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes longitudinal comparisons (e.g., Argentina: interest in news has fallen 32 points since 2017). Useful for assessing long-term engagement and shifts in public attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country and market-level data comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Country and market data — interactive, comparable measures across 47 countries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report provides country-by-country breakdowns (Europe, North America, Latin America, Asia Pacific, Africa) enabling cross-market comparisons by demographics and other segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological transparency and sample representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Research was conducted by YouGov (and their partners) using an online questionnaire in January and February 2024, based on a YouGov survey of more than 95,000 people in 47 countries representing half of the world's population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing, provider, sample size and country coverage — criteria for assessing the validity, reliability and representativeness of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accessibility and interactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Build your own charts with our interactive. Compare data from different markets and demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises availability of interactive tools, downloadable PDF and slide presentation, and other resources (podcast, launch events) to explore and reuse the data — a standard for transparency and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supplementary qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary report commissioned ('OK computer?') based on qualitative research by strategic insight agency Craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines quantitative survey results with qualitative findings to provide richer interpretation of attitudes (especially on AI); a criterion for mixed-methods robustness.
